headline: GOLD SOARS 3RD STRAIGHT SESSION: TRUMP IRAN TRUCE TALK LIFTS METAL TOWARD $4,179 WITH CPI TOMORROW
snippet: Gold has now rallied for three consecutive sessions from its 7-month low of $4,060, with XAU/USD climbing toward $4,179 after U.S. President Donald Trump signalled the U.S. and Iran could sign a ceasefire deal 'as soon as the weekend,' reducing the oil-surge inflation premium that has been the primary gold headwind since Iran-US hostilities escalated in early July. With September rate-hike odds falling below 63% and the June CPI print due at 8:30 a.m. ET on July 14, precious metals are entering the most consequential 24 hours of Q3 from a position of momentum rather than defensive selling.

headline: SILVER UP TODAY: IRAN CEASEFIRE SIGNALS SHIFT THE FED'S RATE CALCULUS — SEPTEMBER HIKE ODDS FALL BELOW 60%
snippet: GoldSilver.com's July 13 analysis explains why silver is outperforming gold in today's session: Trump's Iran truce language is the specific catalyst that has altered Fed-watcher arithmetic — when an Iran ceasefire removes the oil-price component of elevated CPI, the mechanical case for a September rate hike collapses faster than the general inflation narrative, and silver benefits disproportionately because industrial demand is already supplying a $59–62 floor while the investment bid was entirely absent. The Fed's 9-to-8 split means only one committee member needs to flip, and falling rate-hike odds are the trigger.

headline: GDX/GDXJ LOG BEST SINGLE-SESSION GAINS IN MONTHS — MINING ETFS SURGE AS PRECIOUS METALS RALLY ACCELERATES
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) and VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) are posting their largest single-session percentage gains in months as the gold price rebound extends into a third consecutive day, with GDXJ's 52-week gain extending toward 80% and the equity leverage trade amplifying each dollar of gold recovery into 3–4x EBITDA improvement at current all-in sustaining costs of approximately $1,725/oz against $4,100+ gold. The combination of compressed COMEX net-long positioning (194,000 contracts, down 13% from January's crowded peak) and Iran-deal-driven rate-fear reduction is providing the cleaner technical backdrop that gold equities needed to break their disconnect from metal price.

headline: IS ASIA ABOUT TO CHANGE GOLD FOREVER? PBOC BUYS MOST SINCE 2023 IN JUNE — HONG KONG CHALLENGES LBMA FOR PRICE DISCOVERY
snippet: Money Metals' July 11 analysis argues that Asian institutional demand — led by the PBOC's 14.93-tonne June purchase (the largest single-month addition since 2023, extending the buying streak to 20 consecutive months) and Hong Kong's new gold settlement platform targeting the London Bullion Market Association's dominant price-discovery role — is structurally decoupling gold from Western ETF flow dominance. With 45% of surveyed central banks globally now planning to increase their gold reserves over the next 12 months (a record high), the price floor mechanisms operating independently of Federal Reserve policy are more durable than at any point in the prior gold bull market cycle.

headline: GOLDSEEK: THE BUSY WEEK AHEAD — CPI AND WARSH TESTIMONY WILL RESOLVE GOLD'S 6-MONTH SETUP IN 48 HOURS
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly preview identifies two events that will resolve gold's six-month consolidation range in a 48-hour window: June CPI at 8:30 a.m. ET July 14 (with the Cleveland Fed's inflation nowcast calling for a rare negative monthly headline reading of -0.1% driven by crude oil's retreat toward $68/barrel) and Fed Chair Warsh's first congressional testimony as part of the Fed's Semiannual Monetary Policy Report. A soft CPI plus balanced Warsh statement is the 'squeeze setup' that clears the primary mechanical headwind at the 194,000-contract COMEX net-long level; a CPI beat at 4.2%+ year-over-year extends gold's consolidation below $4,150 into late July.

headline: GOLD UPDATE #869: 'RALLY IS NIGH?' TECHNICAL BUY SIGNALS FIRED AT $4,049 — WAR STILL SUPPRESSING MOMENTUM
snippet: Mark Mead Baillie's 869th Gold Update (July 11, Monte-Carlo) documents that technical buy signals — the 'Baby Blues' regression trend indicators — fired for gold on July 2 at $4,049 and for silver a day earlier on July 1 at $59.25, with both metals now trading above their buy points despite the Iran war repeatedly suppressing momentum rallies. Gold's intraweek range of $4,033 to $4,216 demonstrates both the upward technical impulse and the war-inflation mechanism that collapses rallies; the title question 'Gold Rally Is Nigh?' hinges on whether the CPI print on July 14 finally removes the hawkish Fed narrative that has been overriding the technical buy signal since early July.

headline: CAN SILVER RETURN ABOVE $100 IN 2026 IF THE US-IRAN CONFLICT ENDS? THE MATH FOR A 65% MOVE
snippet: TradingKey's July 13 silver forecast analysis maps the mechanism for silver reclaiming $100+: an Iran ceasefire removes oil-driven CPI inflation → September rate-hike probability collapses below 30% → real yields fall → the $59–62 silver floor becomes the launch pad rather than the ceiling. Silver's historical leverage ratio to gold (currently compressed near 65:1 from its long-run average of 40–50:1) means a gold recovery toward $5,000 mechanically targets $75–100 silver even without any investment demand re-entry, while industrial demand from solar, EVs, and data-centre power infrastructure provides a demand floor that operates regardless of Fed policy.

headline: MALAYSIA RACES TO BUILD NON-CHINA HEAVY REE SUPPLY: LYNAS, JS LINK AND CARESTER ALL COMMIT IN SAME WEEK
snippet: The REEx Structural Rare Earth Market Signal Tracker for the week of July 6–11 identifies Malaysia as the focal point of the Western world's race to build non-China rare earth separation and permanent magnet manufacturing: Lynas Rare Earths and South Korea's JS Link advanced permanent magnet manufacturing at the Kuantan facility, while Carester announced plans for a new major separation plant in Malaysia — all within the same week. The REEx Structural Momentum Index rose from 5.9 to 6.1, but the report cautions that China's leverage actually increased through tighter export controls, and Japanese manufacturers are warning of heavy REE shortages with no non-Chinese supply adequate to replace restricted dysprosium and terbium volumes.

headline: WARSH SAT OUT THE DOT PLOT — FOMC MINUTES DROP WEDNESDAY: WHAT THEY REVEAL ABOUT GOLD'S Q3 FATE
snippet: GoldSilver.com's preview of the July 15 FOMC meeting minutes release — the first published under Chair Warsh — explains why these minutes are uniquely significant for gold investors: Warsh notably declined to submit his own rate forecast for the committee's Summary of Economic Projections, meaning the minutes are the first public window into his actual views on inflation and the pace of potential rate hikes. A minutes release showing Warsh's committee leaning toward patience rather than immediate hikes on the back of June CPI weakness would be the second consecutive dovish signal this week after the CPI print itself, a combination that historically accelerates gold's repricing in Q3.
